KR-N05.decision: the three properties are enforced by mechanism and were exercised in practice. No infinite loop: max_model_turns / max_run_duration / max_total_tokens bound every run, and this goal run was paused for a decision rather than spinning. No authority widening: the live provider spend required an explicit --max-tokens envelope (a 2000-token attempt was refused before dispatch) and is now recorded in live_total_budget + operator_authorization. No blocked-to-done: four items are BLOCKED_EXTERNAL with probe evidence (blocked_probes.md) and 35 experiments are DEFERRED rather than relabelled, even though that is what an auditor is pushing for.

KR-N06.decision: the two properties the task names are covered. Side-effect boundaries stay explainable after a disturbance: gate5 aborts in-flight workers on timeout and on parent cancellation and cleans up their isolated worktrees (parallel fan-out, conflict detection and post-merge verify-failure revert are in the same target), and durable_tasks::restart_recovery_marks_a_started_task_unknown_and_refuses_resume is exactly "an unknown state is not silently re-run as a write" -- the task becomes unknown and refuses to resume rather than repeating side effects. No resource leak: job_scope reclaims recorded child groups and the arm reports surviving pids as an unknown verdict instead of a pass. Not covered: a dedicated kill -9 stress loop against a live worker tree; the recovery semantics above are the mechanism that would handle it, but the loop itself was not written.

KR-P03.decision: the daemon already bounds this: a 16-permit semaphore drops the stream when try_acquire_owned fails (no queue), and connections idle past 60s are terminated. Added connection_ownership::connections_beyond_the_cap_are_refused_not_queued, which holds all 16 permits and then requires the next sockets to be closed (EOF/error) rather than served. Existing b02_idle_timeout_terminates_quiet_connection_without_active_run and acp_owner_run_completion_releases_its_connection_permit cover the other two halves: a quiet client is reaped, and permits are not leaked. Measured, not a constant reading.

KR-P04.decision: validate_daemon_listen_endpoint strictly rejects non-loopback TCP binds (0.0.0.0, LAN IPs, [::]) unless a non-empty --auth-token is configured, so a plaintext control plane cannot be exposed by accident; test_daemon_non_loopback_warning_emitted_and_does_not_leak_token covers the warning path and that the token is not echoed, and connection_ownership covers unauthenticated refusal. CAPABILITIES.md states plainly that the transport is plaintext and must only be used on a trusted network, which is the explicit deployment contract the task asks for.

KR-P05.decision: terminal safety and accessibility are covered by tests, not by intent: repl_terminal_ux::approval_prompt_escapes_untrusted_arguments and untrusted_diagnostic_labels_are_escaped (a tool argument or diagnostic cannot inject escape sequences into the prompt), display_width_and_truncation_are_unicode_and_ansi_aware and startup_banner_lines_fit_the_terminal_width (wide CJK and narrow terminals render without breaking the layout), plus gate9_zen_tui for theme switching, status fields and diff rendering. Interruptibility is covered on the same surface by the approval/cancel paths in gate6 (test_rpc_approval_pause_and_resume_approve_and_deny_and_disconnect_fail_closed) and the ACP cancel notification test.

KR-P06.decision: the ACP surface is exercised through raw JSON-RPC from a client that does not use Kroma internals, which is what "independent client" means here: acp_contract covers initialize negotiation, prompt with content blocks and streamed updates, non-conformant request rejection, standard permission request gating a tool, and a cancel notification yielding a cancelled stop reason; gate6 adds the full stdio flow (test_acp_stdio_initialize_prompt_event_stream_and_evidence_recall) and test_rpc_approval_pause_and_resume_approve_and_deny_and_disconnect_fail_closed for approve/deny/disconnect. Not claimed: interop with a third-party IDE or desktop client.

KR-Q02.decision: self_repair_guard::protected_artifacts() protects exactly what the task names: tool/policy.rs (the permission ceiling), bench.rs (scorer and paired/cluster statistics), completion_gate.rs (what counts as done), ahe.rs (self-repair verdict rules), experiment.rs (promotion rules), the whole crates/kroma-core/tests/ prefix (a candidate that can edit the suite can edit its grade), provenance.rs, secure_fs.rs, sandbox.rs, the guard itself, and the release trust root plus signing tool. check() refuses a candidate touching any of them, including a protected file inside an allowed prefix (self_repair_guard::protected_artifacts_are_refused_even_inside_an_allowed_prefix), and t19_ahe_isolation exercises the isolation end to end. Keys are covered by path protection plus the existing credential scrub; a candidate cannot lower the standard it is graded against.

KR-Q03.decision: dependency and license inventory generated from the workspace manifests; no vendored upstream sources under crates/

KR-Q04.decision: added tool_contracts::hostile_argument_bodies_are_refused_without_panicking: 14 adversarial bodies (truncated JSON, null, array, scalar, wrong types, bad array items, duplicate keys, control characters, 40-deep nesting, oversized, trailing garbage, __proto__) all return a structured refusal under 512 bytes or a legitimate pass, with no panic and no allocation blow-up; four classes are spot-asserted so the loop cannot pass vacuously. Other trusted boundaries already carry adversarial tests: filesystem_security (path escape), mcp_http_2026 (hostile schema, forged headers, non-loopback plaintext), b13/t09/t31 sandbox suites.

KR-Q05.decision: least data by default: the run log carries prompt_hash and never the prompt text (t03::the_event_log_does_not_contain_the_prompt_in_plaintext), tool output is bounded by inline caps plus spill budgets (t06_bounded_io), credential-shaped host variables are scrubbed from every child (b08_shared_launch::one_shot_launch_scrubs_secret_environment), and the daemon does not echo the auth token in its non-loopback warning (gate6 test_daemon_non_loopback_warning_emitted_and_does_not_leak_token). Diagnostics never require carrying source or credentials: the latency/IO reports use byte counts and hashes.
